To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified a number of differentially expressed miRNA species in metastatic versus non-metastastic prostate cancer xenografted into mice, and that some of the differentially expressed species have been previously reported to be differentially expressed in human metastatic versus non metastatic prostate cancer.
we used a novel approach to identify miRNAs that may be potential biomarkers or therapeutic targets for prostate cancers with metastasis.

the use of metastatic versus non-metastastic xenografts from one patient's prostate cancer allowed us to identify 36 novel and known miRNAs that were differentially expressed, some of which are potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets for prostate cancers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of miRNAs that are associated with prostate cancer metastasis.
the identification of novel biomarkers and therapeutic targets for metastatic prostate cancer, a disease that remains incurable.
the identification of biomarkers and novel targets for prostate cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the results presented in this study provide a basis for further studies aimed to validate the potential of the differentially expressed prostate cancer-associated miRNAs identified herein as novel biomarkers for prostate cancer metastases, and as potential therapeutic targets for the disease.
this work provides a list of potential biomarkers and novel targets for prostate cancer.
the results of this study provide the basis for a hypothesis to be tested in a larger study, and that this study provides a methodology that can be used to test this hypothesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the identification of miRNAs associated with prostate cancer metastasis may provide new insights into the biology of the disease and new biomarkers or therapeutic targets.

the use of subrenal capsule xenotransplantation of prostate cancer tissue from the same patient into mice, followed by RNA sequencing of the resulting metastatic and non- metastatic prostate cancer lines, can be a powerful approach to identifying potential biomarkers for and/or therapeutic targets of prostate cancer metastasis.

the use of metastatic versus non-metastastic subrenal capsule xenograph lines derived from one patient’s cancer makes it likely the differentially expressed microRNAs identified in our study include potential biomarker and/or therapeutic target for human prostate cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that

miRNAs can be identified that are differentially expressed in metastatic versus non-metastastic cancers, and that these miRNAs are likely to be involved in metastasis and/or other aspects of cancer progression.
metastatic and nonmetastatic prostate cancers are characterized by distinct miRNA profiles.

miRNA expression profiles in prostate cancer xenografted into NOD/SCI mice are similar to those of the original patient's cancer and that the miRNAs identified may be useful biomarkers and/or potential therapeutic targets for human metastatic prostate cancer.
